# tacsim's integration test targets (one per crates/tacsim/tests/*.rs), split
# across the `test` job's `tacsim-integration-N` shards in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
# `scripts/ci-tacsim-shard.sh N` runs line N as `cargo nextest run -P ci -p tacsim
# --test ...` (nextest since cut T.1, 2026-10-26: the shard's binaries in one pool).
#
# Since test-strategy cut T.3 (2026-10-26) the targets are the six group
# binaries shard_1..shard_6 — tests/shard_N.rs, one `mod` line per former
# tests/<name>.rs, which now lives at tests/shard_N/<name>.rs — plus harness
# and cost_lane, which stay targets of their own (a crate-root-only
# `#![recursion_limit]`; an exclusive timing lock and a script-parity test).
# Each group IS its shard. Six since 2026-10-27, balanced on the per-module
# test times of main's run 40428411078 (the JUnit testcases' `<module>::`
# prefix): 46.4, 47.4, 46.7, 47.7, 48.7 and 45.0 summed minutes per shard,
# harness (0.9) and cost_lane (6.4) counted with theirs, against 65-74 as four;
# then, the same day, cost_lane weighted FOURFOLD, because it runs alone
# (.config/nextest.toml: threads-required = the whole pool, so its minutes
# are serial, and shard_2 ran at parallelism 2.4 against 3.5-4 elsewhere, the
# wall of both PR runs): unloading (9.5) to shard_6 and deposits (7.2) to
# shard_3, for 46.4, 30.7 (49.9 with cost_lane's three idle threads), 53.9,
# 47.7, 48.7 and 54.5. A run-alone binary's minutes count once per thread.
# The three named #[ignore]d mind-hash tests (minds_pool, minds_rhai, twin) sit
# together in shard_2 and run in the `tacsim-minds` matrix cell, not here.
#
# Every target must appear on exactly one line:
# crates/mush-contract-tests/tests/ci_tacsim_shards.rs fails on a missing,
# doubled or unknown target, so a new top-level test file cannot silently go
# unrun. A new test MODULE is a `mod` line in one of the six shard roots and
# runs with that shard. Rebalance by moving a `mod` line between two shard
# roots when a shard drifts far from the others (per-module times: the JUnit
# report's testcases, whose names carry the `<module>::` prefix).
1: shard_1 harness
2: shard_2 cost_lane
3: shard_3
4: shard_4
5: shard_5
6: shard_6
